mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals strengthening demand-side conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity picks up.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales of domestic product (RSAFS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for two consecutive months.
